newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GUNMAN HITS VICTIM OVER HEAD IN NEW BUDAPEST ATTACK.
newsitem.headline: GUNMAN HITS VICTIM OVER HEAD IN NEW BUDAPEST ATTACK.

text.p: Budapest's spate of armed attacks on businessmen continued on Friday morning when an unknown attacker first shot at a Budapest casino owner and then hit him on the head with the gun.

Police officer Gyorgy Molnar, who inspected the site, told Hungarian news agency MTI the businessman was getting out of his jeep outside his home when the masked man fired at him from a small-bore pistol.
The bullet missed its target and lodged against the door of a nearby parked car.
Molnar said the weapon may then have failed, prompting the assailant to knock his victim down with his gun before fleeing.
The 52-year-old businessman, identified only by his initials S. D., was taken into hospital.

Budapest has been rocked for the past two months by a gangland turf war that has included more than a dozen hand grenade attacks on nightclubs and restaurants and at least four other shootings, one of them fatal.
Businessman Zoltan Csapo, 56, was shot repeatedly by an attacker on a motorcycle who turned in front of the victim's jeep and fired at him on Tuesday evening.

Jozsef Prisztas, a known underworld figure, was shot dead at the wheel of his car on November 1. He has been linked to an underworld "banker", Andras Lakatos, who reportedly absconded to Mexico with billions of forints of underworld money.
Budapest Police Commander Janos Bodracska was relieved of his day-to-day duties on Thursday in a move seen as stemming from his failure to solve the spate of shootings and bombings.
His powers have been extended to the entire territory of Hungary from December 1.
